source.author: lucan
source.text: Iliacae quoque signa manus, perituraque castra Ominibus petiere suis: nec fabula Troiae Continuit, Phrygiique ferens se Caesar Iuli.
source.text_original: Iliacae quoque signa manus, perituraque castra / Ominibus petiere suis: nec fabula Troiae / Continuit, Phrygiique ferens se Caesar Iuli.
source.text_english: The hands of Ilium too sought out their standards and their doomed camp by their own omens; nor did the tale of Troy hold him back, Caesar, bearing himself as a Phrygian Iulus.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: Phoebe, mone, si Cymaeae mihi conscia vatis stat casta cortina domo, si laurea digna fronte viret; tuque o, pelagi cui maior aperti fama, Caledonius postquam tua carbasa vexit Oceanus Phrygios prius indignatus Iulos, eripe me populis et habenti nubila terrae, sancte pater, veterumque fave veneranda canenti facta virum.
reuse.text_original: Phoebe, mone, si Cymaeae mihi conscia vatis / stat casta cortina domo, si laurea digna / fronte viret; tuque o, pelagi cui maior aperti / fama, Caledonius postquam tua carbasa vexit / Oceanus Phrygios prius indignatus Iulos, / eripe me populis et habenti nubila terrae, / sancte pater, veterumque fave veneranda canenti / facta virum.
reuse.text_english: Phoebus, give me guidance, if the chaste tripod of the Cumaean prophetess stands as a witness in my house, if the laurel grows green on a brow worthy of it; and you, whose fame is greater over the open sea, since Caledonian Ocean bore your sails after, in anger, it had first borne the Phrygian Iulii, rescue me from the peoples and from the earth that holds the clouds, holy father, and favor the ancient deeds of men, while I sing them in reverence.
